title: Describing Data
description: Summarize datasets using center and spread, then interpret simple charts.

lessons.title: Mean, Median, and Mode
objectives: Compute mean, median, and mode for small datasets
Choose an appropriate center measure for different data shapes

pedagogy.title: Sort first for median
pedagogy.content: Always sort the numbers before finding the median.

pedagogy.title: Check for outliers
pedagogy.content: If one value is very extreme, median may represent the center better than mean.

content.content: The mean is the average, the median is the middle value of sorted data, and the mode is the most frequent value.

exercises.question: Find the mean of 3, 5, 7, 9.
hints: Divide by the number of values (4).

exercises.question: Compute the median of 12, 4, 8, 20, 16 and explain your steps.
hints: Pick the middle value after sorting.
exercises.solution: Self-check: sorted data is 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 so the median is 12.

lessons.title: Range and Data Displays
objectives: Compute range as a measure of spread
Interpret bar charts and simple frequency tables

pedagogy.title: Range = max minus min
pedagogy.content: Range is the largest value minus the smallest value.

pedagogy.title: Axis labels matter
pedagogy.content: Always check chart axes and category labels before drawing conclusions.

content.content: Spread shows how far data values vary. The range is a quick spread measure.

content.prompt: Sketch a bar chart for study hours: Mon=1, Tue=2, Wed=2, Thu=3, Fri=1.

exercises.question: Find the range of 14, 9, 21, 11, 18.
hints: Identify the largest and smallest values.

exercises.question: Draw a bar chart for pets owned by five students: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3. Label axes.
exercises.solution: Self-check: bars should show frequencies: 0->1, 1->2, 2->1, 3->1 with labeled axes.
